proofs.verified_behavior: For the constructed proof-side finite-slice cursor (remaining=len, one-byte chunk, advance=drop one; unused Buf fields are error stubs), the translated default succeeds when the destination fits the unread slice, returns exactly that prefix, and leaves the corresponding suffix. The one-byte callback law applies on each nonempty loop iteration, so the result covers repeated chunks. This is a Lean model instance, not a proof about any concrete Rust Buf implementation.
assumptions: Destination length is at most the input finite-slice cursor length
